mainTopic: The מצוות of בני נח: תורה study by a גוי, דם מן החי, and which early מצוות still bind the nations
overview: The amud opens by explaining that דינין has both a 'do' side and a 'don't' side, so it fits the list of seven מצוות of בני נח. Then רבי יוחנן rules that a גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה, because the תורה is our מורשה. The גמרא explains that this ban falls under גזל, or under the law of a נערה המאורסה. A ברייתא of רבי מאיר seems to clash with this, and the גמרא answers that רבי מאיר praises only a גוי who learns his own seven מצוות. Next, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל adds a ban on דם מן החי, and the גמרא shows how he and the רבנן each read the פסוקים. This leads to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule. A מצוה given to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both groups, while one not repeated applies only to ישראל. The גמרא defends both halves, using עבודה זרה and the principle that nothing is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי. The amud ends by quoting the first half of the rule again, setting up a challenge on 59b.

steps.title: But courts are an active מצוה, and they are still counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the seven מצוות only list 'sit and don't do' מצוות, because דינין is an active מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But setting up courts is a 'get up and do' מצוה, and the list still counts it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had just said that the list of seven מצוות only counts 'don't do' מצוות. Now it pushes back: דינין is something you must actively do, yet it is on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list really counted only שב ואל תעשה מצוות, an active מצוה like דינין should not appear on it. Its presence seems to break the rule the גמרא just gave.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of justice: the מצוה for בני נח to set up courts
'Get up and do': an active, positive מצוה

phrases.english: But courts of justice are a 'get up and do' מצוה,
and yet he counts it?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא who listed the seven מצוות of בני נח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim from the previous section that the list counts only 'don't do' מצוות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the seven מצוות list only counts שב ואל תעשה מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דינין is an active מצוה, yet it appears on the list, so the rule seems wrong.

steps.title: Courts include both a 'do' and a 'don't'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that דינין has both an active side and a 'refrain' side.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are both 'get up and do' and 'sit and don't do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דינין is not only an active מצוה. It also has a 'don't do' side, so it still fits the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The active side is the duty to set up courts and judge. The 'don't do' side is the ban on doing injustice. Because of that 'don't' side, דינין still fits a list of שב ואל תעשה מצוות.

phrases.aramaic: קוּם עֲשֵׂה וְשֵׁב אַל תַּעֲשֶׂה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: They are both 'get up and do' and 'sit and don't do.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קוּם עֲשֵׂה וְשֵׁב אַל תַּעֲשֶׂה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the מצוה as having two sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דינין is only an active מצוה, so it should not be on a 'don't do' list.
steps.terutzMaskana: דינין also has a 'don't do' side, so it belongs on the list.

steps.title: A גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה, because the תורה is 'our inheritance.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: a גוי who learns תורה deserves death, since the פסוק says 'משה commanded us the תורה as an inheritance.' It is an inheritance for us, not for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי יוחנן. He rules that a גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word לנו ('to us') in the פסוק. The תורה was given as a מורשה, an inheritance belonging to כלל ישראל and not to other nations.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the next two questions: why it is not on the list of seven, and how it fits with רבי מאיר's teaching.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
A non-Jew who learns Torah is liable to death,
as it says: 'Moshe commanded us the Torah, an inheritance,'
an inheritance for us, and not for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about another prohibition for בני נח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה, based on the word מורשה.

steps.title: Then why is this not counted with the seven מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this prohibition is not on the list of seven מצוות of בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the list count it along with the seven מצוות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רבי יוחנן. If learning תורה is forbidden to a גוי on pain of death, why is it missing from the list of seven?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of seven is supposed to cover the prohibitions of בני נח. A separate ban that carries death would seem to make the list incomplete. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven מצוות of בני נח

phrases.english: So let him count it along with the seven מצוות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death-penalty prohibition for בני נח should appear on the list of seven, but it does not.

steps.title: It falls under robbery, or under the law of a betrothed girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ban is already inside an existing category: גזל if you read the word as מורשה, or the עריות of a נערה המאורסה if you read it as מאורסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who reads it as 'inheritance' says the גוי is stealing it, which is גזל. The one who reads it as 'betrothed' says his law is like that of a betrothed girl, which is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that this ban is not a new, separate מצוה. It is already part of one of the seven, and it gives two ways to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word is מורשה, the תורה belongs to כלל ישראל, so a גוי who takes it is committing גזל, which is already one of the seven. If the word is read as מאורסה, the תורה is like a bride promised to כלל ישראל, so it falls under עריות, and the punishment matches that of a נערה המאורסה: סקילה.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'betrothed' reading is a play on the spelling of the same word in the פסוק. It is not a different פסוק.

phrases.english: The one who says 'inheritance':
he is stealing it.
The one who says 'betrothed':
phrases.notes: He reads the word מורשה as if it said מאורסה, since the two words look and sound alike.

phrases.english: his law is like a betrothed girl, which is by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר ״מוֹרָשָׁה״ מִיגְזָל קָא גָזֵיל לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the case inside an existing category (two readings)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning תורה is a separate, eighth prohibition that is missing from the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is already included under גזל or under עריות, depending on how you read the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי learning תורה is not an eighth מצוה. It falls under גזל (מורשה) or under עריות (מאורסה).

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a גוי who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר praises a גוי who learns תורה as being like a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: רבי מאיר used to say, how do we know that even a גוי who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול? Because the פסוק says 'which a man does and lives by them.' It does not say כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, but 'a man.' So even a גוי who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a strong question on רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. This step only sets up the problem, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the word האדם ('a man') as including all people, not only Jews. That makes a גוי who learns תורה greatly praised, which seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's ruling that he is חייב מיתה.

phrases.english: They challenged: Rabbi Meir used to say:
From where do we know that even a non-Jew who learns Torah
is like a High Priest?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם הָאָדָם וָחַי בָּהֶם״.
phrases.english: As it says: 'which a man shall do and live by them.'
It does not say 'Kohanim, Levi'im, and Yisraelim,'
but rather 'a man.'

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: So you have learned that even a non-Jew who learns Torah
is like a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to challenge רבי יוחנן's basic ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a גוי who learns תורה is חייב מיתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר reads האדם as including a גוי and praises a גוי who learns תורה as being like a כהן גדול, which clashes with a death penalty.

steps.title: The praised גוי learns only his own seven מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר praises a גוי only when he learns the laws of the seven מצוות of בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the ברייתא is talking about a גוי who learns his own seven מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6. רבי מאיר's praise is only for a גוי who learns the laws of his own seven מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן forbids a גוי to learn תורה in general, and רבי מאיר praises a גוי who learns. Both can be true: learning the seven מצוות that apply to him is praiseworthy, while learning the rest of the תורה is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other source (the ברייתא of רבי מאיר)
The seven מצוות commanded to all בני נח

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי may learn and is praised for learning the laws of his own seven מצוות‎. רבי יוחנן's prohibition covers the rest of the תורה.

phrases.english: There, it is speaking of their own seven מצוות.
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא where רבי מאיר compared the learning גוי to a כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by narrowing the case in רבי מאיר's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the praised learning is only of the seven מצוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר praises any תורה learning by a גוי, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's praise covers only the seven מצוות of בני נח, so there is no contradiction with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Opening a new topic: blood from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי חנינא בן גמליאל from the list of מצוות of בני נח: blood from a living animal is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: also blood from a living animal is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the ברייתא that listed the מצוות of בני נח. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל adds a prohibition beyond the standard seven: a בן נח may not eat blood taken from an animal while it is still alive. The next steps look for the source of this view.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds extra prohibitions for בני נח
Blood taken from a living animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:
Also blood from a living animal is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף הַדָּם מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the topic of a גוי learning תורה is closed, the גמרא moves to the next opinion in the list of מצוות of בני נח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, בני נח are also forbidden to eat blood from a living animal.

steps.title: The ברייתא and its פסוק about eating from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק about flesh with its life as forbidding אבר מן החי, and רבי חנינא בן גמליאל adds that it also forbids blood from a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.' This is a limb from a living animal. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: also blood from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows where רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's opinion comes from. Both sides learn from the same פסוק said to נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees this פסוק forbids eating a limb from a living animal. The argument is only whether the word 'its blood' adds a second prohibition, blood from a living animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut off from a living animal
With its life, while it is still alive

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Only flesh with its life, which is its blood, you shall not eat":
This is a limb from a living animal.
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:
Also blood from a living animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַךְ בָּשָׂר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ דָמוֹ לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא and the פסוק behind the opinion quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק forbids אבר מן החי to בני נח. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds that it also forbids דם מן החי.

steps.title: What is רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא בן גמליאל gets a prohibition of blood out of this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא בן גמליאל reads the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance the פסוק seems to say one thing: flesh with its life, which is its blood. The גמרא wants to know how he finds a separate ban on blood in it.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reading of the פסוק behind רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק teaches a separate ban on blood from a living animal.

steps.title: Reading the פסוק as two separate prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל reads 'with its life' as going on both 'flesh' and 'its blood', which gives two prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read the פסוק this way: 'Flesh with its life you shall not eat,' and 'Its blood with its life you shall not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he splits the פסוק into two commands. 'With its life' is read together with 'flesh' and also together with 'its blood'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Flesh with its life' is אבר מן החי. 'Its blood with its life' is דם מן החי. One פסוק therefore yields two separate bans.

keyTerms.meaning: Read it as, read into the פסוק

phrases.english: Read into it:
"Flesh with its life you shall not eat,"
"its blood with its life you shall not eat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word בנפשו is read with both בשר and דמו, which makes two prohibitions: אבר מן החי and דם מן החי.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use the word 'its blood'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the word 'its blood', since they do not forbid blood from a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the word 'its blood' in the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not forbid blood from a living animal to בני נח. But the word 'its blood' is still written in the פסוק, so it must teach them something.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן, how do they explain it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: what do the רבנן do with the word 'its blood' in the פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's reading, the גמרא asks for the other side's use of the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word דמו teaches according to the רבנן.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'its blood' permits creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the word 'its blood' teaches that a limb from a living שרץ is permitted to בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word comes to permit שרצים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use 'its blood' for a different lesson. It teaches that the ban on a limb from a living animal does not apply to שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, 'its blood' is not a new prohibition. It limits the ban on אבר מן החי, so the creeping creatures it excludes are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what it comes to teach

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same פסוק. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל reads 'its blood' as an extra ban on blood from a living animal. The רבנן read it as excluding שרצים from the ban on אבר מן החי.

phrases.english: That comes to permit creeping animals.
phrases.notes: He means a limb taken from a living שרץ is allowed. The גמרא explains why a little later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use the word דמו to exclude שרצים from the ban on אבר מן החי.

steps.title: A matching reading of a פסוק for the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the פסוק in דברים is read the same way, with one part forbidding אבר מן החי and the other forbidding דם מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way you say: 'Only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life.' 'Only be strong not to eat the blood': this is a limb from a living animal. 'For the blood is the life': this is blood from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a similar reading of a פסוק in דברים. That פסוק is also split into two parts: one forbids a limb from a living animal and the other forbids blood from a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's approach of finding two prohibitions in one פסוק. Here the פסוק was said to the Jewish people, so the same pair of bans appears for them too.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the first part of the פסוק mentions 'the blood', the ברייתא reads it as forbidding a limb from a living animal. The second part, 'for the blood is the life', is the one read as forbidding blood from a living animal.

phrases.english: Similarly, you say:
"Only be steadfast in not eating the blood,
as the blood is the life, etc."
"Only be steadfast in not eating the blood":
this is a limb from a living animal;
"as the blood is the life":
this is blood from a living animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 9 with a parallel two-part reading of a פסוק for the Jewish people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in דברים 12:23 is split into two: one part forbids אבר מן החי and the other forbids דם מן החי.

steps.title: The רבנן apply the פסוק to דם הקזה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the words 'the blood is the life' as teaching the prohibition of דם הקזה, blood through which the life goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they read it? That phrase comes to teach about blood of bloodletting, since the life goes out with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly asks how the רבנן read the פסוק and answers right away. For them, it is about blood let out in bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל used this phrase to forbid blood from a living animal. The רבנן do not hold of that prohibition, so they need another use for the words. They say it teaches about דם הקזה, because that is blood that carries the animal's life out of its body.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the חכמים who argue with רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
The life or soul of the animal

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That phrase
phrases.notes: This is a short question: how do the רבנן read the פסוק from step 14?

phrases.english: is for the blood of bloodletting
since the life goes out with it
that is what it comes to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same phrase that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל used for blood from a living animal
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches the prohibition of דם הקזה, blood through which the life departs

steps.title: Why say the law to בני נח and repeat it at סיני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah states this prohibition for בני נח and then repeats it at סיני. ישראל are also descendants of נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it written for בני נח, and why do I need it repeated at סיני?
steps.whatsHappening: According to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, the same law shows up twice: once in בראשית for בני נח and again in דברים at סיני. The גמרא asks why both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jews come from נח too. So if the law was already given to all of נח's descendants, repeating it at סיני looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what the second mention adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks why a law is written when it seems unnecessary
הר סיני, where the תורה was given to ישראל

phrases.english: Why do I need it written for the descendants of Noah,
and why do I need it repeated at Sinai?
phrases.notes: The first mention is in בראשית 9:4 and the repeat is in דברים 12:23, the פסוק from step 14.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִיכְתַּב לִבְנֵי נֹחַ, וּלְמָה לִי לְמִשְׁנֵי בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from how each פסוק is read to why the law appears in two places at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The repetition of the prohibition in דברים after it was already said to בני נח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישראל are included in בני נח, so a second command at סיני seems unnecessary

steps.title: Repeated at סיני means it applies to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The answer uses רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule. A מצוה given to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both בני נח and ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. He said: any מצוה said to בני נח and repeated at סיני was said for both this group and that group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a general rule from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. The repeat at סיני shows that the law stays in force for both groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the repeat at סיני, we might have thought the law changed after סיני. The repetition tells us it still applies to the nations and also to ישראל. So the second mention is not extra; it confirms that the law covers both groups.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose rule explains why some מצוות are repeated
For this one and for that one, meaning both בני נח and ישראל

phrases.english: It is like the opinion of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
as Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Any מצוה that was said to the descendants of Noah
and was repeated at Sinai,
was said for this group and for that group.
phrases.notes: He means it applies both to the nations and to the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the law is repeated at סיני
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle that gives the repetition a purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The repeat at סיני seemed extra, since ישראל are already among בני נח
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeat shows the law applies to both בני נח and ישראל
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides which of the early commands still bind the nations after מתן תורה.

steps.title: Not repeated means it applies only to Jews, like גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the rule: a מצוה said to בני נח and not repeated at סיני applies to ישראל and not to בני נח. The only example is גיד הנשה, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה said to בני נח and not repeated at סיני was said for ישראל and not for בני נח. We have only one such case, גיד הנשה, and that is according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule with the opposite case. Then it gives the one example that fits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, גיד הנשה was commanded to יעקב's sons, who still had the status of בני נח. It was not repeated at סיני. Even so, it applies only to ישראל and not to the nations.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which may not be eaten
תנא who holds that יעקב's sons were already commanded about גיד הנשה

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that a law said to בני נח applies only to Jews. The point is that גיד הנשה was given to יעקב's sons while they still counted as בני נח, yet the law belongs only to their descendants, ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: Repeated at סיני means it applies to both groups. Not repeated means it applies only to ישראל. The only example is גיד הנשה, according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: A מצוה said to the descendants of Noah and not repeated at Sinai
was said for the Jewish people and not for the descendants of Noah.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה,
phrases.english: And we have only the sciatic nerve as such a case,
and that is according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה reads בראשית 32:33 as a command already given to יעקב's sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule with the opposite case and its one example
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה given to בני נח and not repeated at סיני applies only to ישראל. The only example is גיד הנשה, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Quoting the first half of the rule again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the first half of the rule: a מצוה said to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Any מצוה that was said to the children of נח and was repeated at סיני was said to both this group and that group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first half of the rule again so that it can examine it. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אמר מר' is how the גמרא signals that it is returning to a source it already quoted, now to look at it closely. Here the source is the rule from Step 17. Nothing new is ruled yet; the line is quoted only so it can be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', the formula for re-quoting an earlier source in order to analyze it
The descendants of נח, meaning all non-Jews
Was repeated at סיני, when the תורה was given
To this one and to that one, meaning both בני נח and ישראל

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the rule of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא from a few lines earlier.

phrases.english: Any מצוה that was said to the children of Noah
and was repeated at Sinai,
was said to this one and to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה לִבְנֵי נֹחַ וְנִשְׁנֵית בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first half of the rule quoted in Step 17 in order to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה said to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both בני נח and ישראל.

steps.title: On the contrary: repeating it should mean only ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite: if a מצוה was repeated at סיני, that should show it was meant only for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Since it was repeated at סיני, it should be said only to ישראל and not to the children of נח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first half of the rule. It says the repetition at סיני could point the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could read the repetition at סיני as moving the מצוה over to ישראל, so that from then on it belongs only to them. On that reading, repeating it would take it away from בני נח instead of confirming it for both groups. The challenge says the rule's reading is not the only possible one.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, which introduces a challenge that flips the logic around
From the fact that, or since

phrases.english: On the contrary, since it was repeated at Sinai –
it was said to Israel and not to the children of Noah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just quoted by drawing the opposite conclusion from the same fact.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first half of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule, that a repeated מצוה applies to both groups.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating a מצוה at סיני could mean it was handed over to ישראל alone, which would take it away from בני נח.

steps.title: Proof from עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: עבודה זרה was repeated at סיני, yet גוים are still punished for it. So a repeated מצוה applies to both groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since עבודה זרה was repeated at סיני, and we find that God punished the גוים for it, learn from this: a repeated מצוה was said to both this group and that group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a real case. עבודה זרה was repeated at סיני, but גוים are still punished for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If repeating a מצוה at סיני took it away from בני נח, then גוים could not be punished for עבודה זרה. Because we find that they are punished for it, repeating it clearly did not remove it from them. This case shows that the rule's reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, the formula for drawing a conclusion

phrases.english: Since idol worship was repeated at Sinai,
and we find that He punished gentiles for it,
learn from it: it was said to this one and to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִיתְּנַי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּסִינַי, וְאַשְׁכְּחַן דַּעֲנַשׁ גּוֹיִם עִילָּוַוהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 and backs up the rule of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating a מצוה at סיני might take it away from בני נח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since גוים are punished for עבודה זרה even though it was repeated, a repeated מצוה applies to both groups.
steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה repeated at סיני applies to both groups. The proof is עבודה זרה: it was repeated, and גוים are still punished for it.

steps.title: Quoting the second half of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes the second half: a מצוה said to בני נח and not repeated at סיני applies to ישראל and not to בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה said to the children of נח and not repeated at סיני was said to ישראל and not to the children of נח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of the rule and quotes it so it can examine it. This is a setup line for the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same second half already seen in Step 18, the case of גיד הנשה. It is quoted again here only so the גמרא can question it. Its result sounds surprising: the מצוה ends up belonging only to ישראל, even though it was first said to בני נח and was never repeated at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said, meaning it was commanded to

phrases.english: To the children of Noah, and not repeated at Sinai –
phrases.notes: The words 'a מצוה that was said' are understood from the first half of the rule.

phrases.english: it was said to Israel and not to the children of Noah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the rule (now proven) to the second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה said to בני נח and not repeated at סיני applies only to ישראל.

steps.title: On the contrary: not repeating it should mean only בני נח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if a מצוה was not repeated at סיני, it should apply only to בני נח, not to ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Since it was not repeated at סיני, it should be said to the children of נח and not to ישראל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second half of the rule. It says the opposite conclusion seems more natural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה never repeated the מצוה at סיני, the plain reading is that it stayed only with the group it was first given to, בני נח. So how can the rule say it belongs to ישראל instead?

keyTerms.meaning: Since not, or from the fact that it did not
הר סיני, where the תורה was given

phrases.english: On the contrary, since it was not repeated at Sinai –
it was said to the children of Noah and not to Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second half of the rule just quoted, in the same way Step 20 attacked the first half.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second half of the rule, that a מצוה not repeated applies only to ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצוה that was never repeated at סיני should naturally stay only with בני נח, the group that first received it.

steps.title: Nothing is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a principle: there is nothing that is allowed for ישראל but forbidden for a גוי. So the מצוה cannot apply to בני נח alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is nothing that is permitted to ישראל and forbidden to a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second half of the rule with a general principle. A גוי can never be held to a stricter standard than a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מצוה applied only to בני נח, the act would be forbidden to a גוי but permitted to a Jew, and that never happens. The first half of the rule already showed that if it applied to both groups, it would have been repeated. So the only option left is that it applies to ישראל alone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the מצוה stays with בני נח. The principle rules that option out, so the מצוה ends up belonging only to ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that a גוי is never more restricted than a Jew, shapes how the גמרא decides who a מצוה applies to.

phrases.english: There is nothing
that is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵיכָּא מִידַּעַם דִּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרֵי וּלְגוֹי אֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle that rules out the alternative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מצוה that was not repeated might apply only to בני נח.
steps.terutzMaskana: That cannot be, because nothing is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי. So the מצוה applies to ישראל.

steps.title: But what about יפת תואר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the principle: יפת תואר is permitted to a Jew but forbidden to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there not? But there is יפת תואר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the principle from the last step with a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish soldier may take a married woman captured in war, a יפת תואר, as a wife. A גוי may not do this. Here, it seems, is something allowed for ישראל but forbidden for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there not? This questions the claim just made
But there is, which brings a counter-example
A woman captured in war, whom the תורה allows a Jewish soldier to marry

phrases.english: And is there not? But there is the beautiful woman!
phrases.notes: This means the woman captured in war, whom a Jewish soldier is allowed to take, even if she was married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle used as the answer in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that nothing is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יפת תואר appears to be exactly such a case: permitted to a Jew, forbidden to a גוי.

steps.title: גוים are not permitted to conquer
steps.stepSummary: יפת תואר is permitted only in a war of conquest, and גוים are not permitted to conquer. So it does not break the principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because they are not people who are permitted to conquer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that יפת תואר is a special case. It does not break the principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission of יפת תואר exists only in a war of conquest. גוים are not permitted to wage such a war, so for them the situation where the permission would apply never comes up. The difference comes from the war, not from a stricter rule about the woman, so the principle still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: יפת תואר does not break the principle that nothing is permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי. The permission depends on a war of conquest, which גוים may not wage.

phrases.english: There, it is because
they are not people permitted to conquer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו בְּנֵי כִיבּוּשׁ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25 and protects the principle of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the counter-example is a different kind of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יפת תואר shows that something can be permitted to a Jew and forbidden to a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission depends on a war of conquest, which גוים may not wage, so the principle still holds.

steps.title: Challenge from stealing less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the principle again: stealing less than a פרוטה seems to be forbidden to a גוי but allowed to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about stealing less than a פרוטה? A גוי may not do it, yet a Jew may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second example that seems to break the rule that nothing is allowed for ישראל but forbidden for a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי is liable for stealing even less than a פרוטה, but for a Jew stealing such a tiny amount is not treated as real stealing. That looks like something allowed for a Jew and forbidden for a גוי. This is exactly what the principle in Step 24 says cannot exist.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (a word that brings a counter-example)
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin that counts in הלכה

phrases.english: But isn't there the case of less than the value of a peruta!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means stealing less than a פרוטה, which a גוי may not do but a Jew may.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the יפת תואר challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a second counter-example to the same principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle from Step 24 that nothing is permitted to ישראל but forbidden to a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stealing less than a פרוטה is forbidden to a גוי and allowed to a Jew, so the principle seems false.

steps.title: גוים do not forgive small amounts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the difference is not in the law itself. A גוי is not the kind of person who forgives even a tiny loss, so taking from him is real stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because they are not people who forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains away the challenge. The difference comes from how people act, not from a stricter law for the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew who loses less than a פרוטה usually lets it go (מחילה), so taking it does not count as stealing. גוים do not forgive even tiny amounts, so for them taking it is a real loss and real stealing. The rule against stealing is the same for both; only the situation is different, so the principle stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgiving or letting go of what someone owes you

phrases.english: There, it is because
they are not people who forgive.
phrases.notes: 'They' means גוים. They don't let go of even a tiny loss, so taking it really hurts them.

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges (יפת תואר and less than a פרוטה) are answered without breaking the principle: nothing is allowed for ישראל but forbidden for a גוי.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו בְּנֵי מְחִילָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the difference comes from people's behavior (forgiving), not from a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stealing less than a פרוטה is allowed for a Jew and forbidden for a גוי, breaking the principle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on stealing is the same; a גוי simply does not forgive tiny amounts, so for him it is real stealing.

steps.title: Quoting the first clause: repeated at סיני applies to both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the first part of the rule: a מצוה said to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both בני נח and ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any מצוה that was said to בני נח and repeated at סיני was said for both this group and that group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule it has been studying and quotes its first clause again. This is a setup line: the challenge on it comes at the start of the next amud (59b).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with מצוות not repeated at סיני. Now the גמרא returns to the other case: a מצוה given to בני נח and given again at סיני. Such a מצוה applies to everyone, Jews and גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: Was repeated (given again) at הר סיני
To this one and to that one (both groups)
Descendants of נח, meaning all non-Jews

phrases.english: Any מצוה that was stated to the descendants of Noah
and was repeated at Sinai,
was stated for this one and for that one.
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means both בני נח and ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִצְוָה שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה לִבְנֵי נֹחַ וְנִישְׁנֵית בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the challenges about the 'not repeated' clause, the גמרא returns to the clause about מצוות that were repeated at סיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה given to בני נח and repeated at סיני applies to both בני נח and ישראל.
